local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local player = Players.LocalPlayer or Players:GetPropertyChangedSignal("LocalPlayer"):Wait()

local KORBLOX_TEXTURE_ID = "rbxassetid://101851254" -- Your requested dark grey texture
local DARK_GREY_COLOR = Color3.fromRGB(64, 64, 64)

local function applyKorblox()
    local char = player.Character
    if not char then return end
    local hum = char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if not hum then return end

    if hum.RigType == Enum.HumanoidRigType.R15 then
        -- R15: MESH SWAP METHOD (Using our successful version)
        local rf = char:FindFirstChild("RightFoot")
        local rl = char:FindFirstChild("RightLowerLeg")
        local ru = char:FindFirstChild("RightUpperLeg")

        if ru and rl and rf then
            rf.Transparency = 1
            rl.Transparency = 1
            
            -- Apply the mesh and texture directly to the MeshPart
            ru.MeshId = "http://www.roblox.com/asset/?id=902942096"
            ru.TextureID = "http://roblox.com/asset/?id=902843398"
            ru.Color = Color3.new(1, 1, 1) -- Set to white so texture isn't tinted
            ru.Transparency = 0
        end
        
    else
        -- R6: SPECIAL MESH METHOD
        local rightLeg = char:FindFirstChild("Right Leg")
        if rightLeg then
            -- Clean out old meshes/CharacterMeshes
            for _, v in ipairs(char:GetChildren()) do
                if v:IsA("CharacterMesh") and v.BodyPart == Enum.BodyPart.RightLeg then
                    v:Destroy()
                end
            end
            
            local mesh = rightLeg:FindFirstChildOfClass("SpecialMesh")
            if not mesh then
                mesh = Instance.new("SpecialMesh")
                mesh.Parent = rightLeg
            end
            
            -- Applying your dark grey settings
            rightLeg.Color = DARK_GREY_COLOR
            rightLeg.Transparency = 0
            
            mesh.MeshType = Enum.MeshType.FileMesh
            mesh.MeshId = KORBLOX_MESH_ID
            mesh.TextureId = KORBLOX_TEXTURE_ID
            mesh.Scale = Vector3.new(1, 1, 1)
        end
    end
end

-- Run continuously to prevent game resets
task.spawn(function()
    while true do
        if player.Character then
            applyKorblox()
        end
        task.wait(0.5)
    end
end)

local function IWJVQ_fake_script() -- MainFrame.LocalScript 
	local script = Instance.new('LocalScript', MainFrame)

	local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
	
	local gui = script.Parent
	
	local dragging
	local dragInput
	local dragStart
	local startPos
	
	local function update(input)
		local delta = input.Position - dragStart
		gui.Position = UDim2.new(startPos.X.Scale, startPos.X.Offset + delta.X, startPos.Y.Scale, startPos.Y.Offset + delta.Y)
	end
	
	gui.InputBegan:Connect(function(input)
		if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
			dragging = true
			dragStart = input.Position
			startPos = gui.Position
	
			input.Changed:Connect(function()
				if input.UserInputState == Enum.UserInputState.End then
					dragging = false
				end
			end)
		end
	end)
	
	gui.InputChanged:Connect(function(input)
		if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
			dragInput = input
		end
	end)
	
	UserInputService.InputChanged:Connect(function(input)
		if input == dragInput and dragging then
			update(input)
		end
	end)
end

🛰️ Smooth Drone V3.4: Immortal Follower
Smooth Drone V3.4 is a high-performance utility script for Roblox, designed to provide players with a sleek, neon-themed companion drone. Unlike standard drone scripts that fly in circles, this version focuses on precision following and utility lighting, ensuring your path is always illuminated with style.
📜 Features & Usage
Intelligent Follow System: The drone stays locked in a fixed position relative to your character (front-right), providing steady lighting without the "spinning" dizziness.
Immortal Re-Spawn Logic: Built-in safety checks automatically recreate the drone if it is destroyed or falls out of the world.
Dynamic UI Console: A draggable and minimizable neon interface allows you to toggle lights and switch colors on the fly.
Rainbow Mode: Activate a cycling RGB effect for both the drone's body and its spotlight.
✅ Pros (Advantages)
Smooth Motion: Uses Lerp (Linear Interpolation) to ensure the drone follows the player with a cinematic, fluid movement rather than snapping instantly.
Camera-Linked Lighting: The spotlight is synchronized with your camera’s LookVector, meaning the drone always shines light exactly where you are looking.
Exploit-Ready UI: The GUI is set to ResetOnSpawn = false, ensuring your controls don't disappear when your character resets.
Physics Stability: By using Anchored = true and manual CFrame updates, the drone avoids glitchy physics collisions that often cause objects to "fling" away.
❌ Cons (Disadvantages)
Client-Side Only: Since this is a LocalScript, other players in the server cannot see your drone or its light; it is for your local experience only.
Manual Color Selection: Currently requires manual clicking to change colors (Green, Red, Blue) rather than a full RGB color picker.
Potential Performance Impact: Because it updates every frame via RenderStepped, users on very low-end mobile devices might experience a slight frame drop if combined with many other heavy scripts.
🚀 How to Use
Copy the provided Lua code.
Paste it into your preferred script executor (e.g., Hydrogen, Delta, or Fluxus).
Execute the script.
